evaluations.evidence: create a new game by entering a name and an optional description
evaluations.rationale: Scope and behavior are concrete and small enough to estimate (UI to create a game with name/description).

evaluations.evidence: invite estimators by giving them a URL
evaluations.rationale: Functionality is specific (generate/share URL) and can be reasonably estimated.

evaluations.evidence: start a round by entering an item in a single multi-line text field
evaluations.rationale: Clear, limited scope (single text field to start round) so estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Viewing list of items is a concrete feature with estimatable scope.

evaluations.evidence: select an item to be estimated or re-estimated
evaluations.rationale: Selection behavior is well scoped and can be estimated.

evaluations.evidence: add an item to the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Adding an item is a narrowly scoped operation that can be estimated.

evaluations.evidence: edit an item in the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Editing items is specific and estimateable without detailed design.

evaluations.evidence: delete an item from the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Deleting an item is a discrete, well-scoped function that can be estimated.

evaluations.evidence: show all estimates immediately
evaluations.rationale: Behavior is specific (show estimates immediately) and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: accept the average of all estimates
evaluations.rationale: Computing and accepting an average is concrete and estimateable.

evaluations.evidence: have the "estimate" field filled in automatically if all estimators show the same card
evaluations.rationale: Acceptance behavior is specific and implementable without detailed design.

evaluations.evidence: enter the agreed-upon estimate
evaluations.rationale: Manual entry of the agreed estimate is a clearly scoped task.

evaluations.evidence: estimate a story we estimated earlier in the session again
evaluations.rationale: Re-estimating a previously estimated item is a specific action suitable for estimation.

evaluations.evidence: import stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Importing from a spreadsheet is a definable feature (format mapping may be needed) and can be reasonably estimated.

evaluations.evidence: copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Copy/paste ingestion is a small, concrete feature that can be estimated.

evaluations.evidence: browse through previous games
evaluations.rationale: Browsing previous games is a clear capability (UI for listing/searching) that can be estimated.

evaluations.evidence: view a transcript of a game
evaluations.rationale: Providing a transcript view is a bounded feature and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a HTML file
evaluations.rationale: Export to HTML is a specific output format and is estimateable.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a CSV file
evaluations.rationale: Export to CSV is a clearly scoped feature and can be estimated.

evaluations.evidence: delete a game, so that stories and estimates for this game are no longer stored
evaluations.rationale: Deleting a game is a discrete operation with clear acceptance and estimateable scope.

evaluations.evidence: create an account ... entering my name, email address, a password and a username
evaluations.rationale: Account creation with listed fields is specific and can be reasonably estimated.

evaluations.evidence: log in using my account name and password
evaluations.rationale: Authentication via name/password is a well-defined feature and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: change my account details
evaluations.rationale: Editing account details is a bounded UI/task and can be estimated.

evaluations.evidence: delete my account
evaluations.rationale: Account deletion (removing account info/games) is a concrete operation that can be estimated.

evaluations.evidence: see dates and times in my local timezone
evaluations.rationale: Timezone display is a defined behavior that is estimateable.

evaluations.evidence: get a password reminder by email
evaluations.rationale: Password reminder via email is a common, bounded feature and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: select whether to have the team estimate with {0, 1/2, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, etc.} or {0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, etc.}
evaluations.rationale: Providing choice of card sets is specific and small enough to estimate.

evaluations.evidence: invite up to 15 estimators
evaluations.rationale: Maximum participants number is explicit; scope is measurable and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: join a game by entering my name on the page I received the URL for
evaluations.rationale: Joining by entering a name via received URL is a concrete action and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: see the item we're estimating
evaluations.rationale: Displaying the current item is specific and estimateable.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we will try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Showing session item list is a concrete UI requirement, suitable for estimation.

evaluations.evidence: immediately see that an estimate has been given by a specific estimator
evaluations.rationale: Indicating who has submitted is clear functionality and can be estimated.

evaluations.evidence: shown all estimates at the same time after all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: Behavior (reveal when all have given) is specific and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: be able to change my estimate up until the last person selects a card and all are shown
evaluations.rationale: Change-until-reveal behavior is precise enough to estimate.

evaluations.evidence: see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
evaluations.rationale: Showing historical estimates for the current story is a defined data/view requirement and estimateable.

evaluations.evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round
evaluations.rationale: Displaying per-estimator votes in current round is specific and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see
evaluations.rationale: A fixed-length visible timer is narrowly scoped and can be estimated.

evaluations.evidence: two-minute timer reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate
evaluations.rationale: Reset-on-condition behavior is specific and can be estimated.

evaluations.evidence: scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds
evaluations.rationale: Providing scroll/navigation through prior rounds is a clear UI feature and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: always have the cards in the same order across multiple draws
evaluations.rationale: Card ordering persistence is a concrete requirement and estimateable.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed
evaluations.rationale: This is a bounded interaction rule and can be estimated.

evaluations.evidence: have a small thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played
evaluations.rationale: Displaying a thumbnail near cards is a specific UI element and estimateable.

evaluations.evidence: site which is compliant with XHTML and CSS standards
evaluations.rationale: Compliance with named standards is a measurable target and can be estimated (tests/changes required).

evaluations.evidence: have a list of definitions for commonly used terms
evaluations.rationale: Creating a glossary is a bounded documentation task and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: created database indexes, so that the queries run as fast as possible
evaluations.rationale: 'as fast as possible' and no indication of which queries to target makes the performance goal open-ended and hard to reasonably estimate.

evaluations.evidence: function correctly in Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2
evaluations.rationale: Supporting specified browser versions is explicit and scopeable for estimation (though may be effortful).

evaluations.evidence: site comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines where possible
evaluations.rationale: Named guidelines provide measurable targets; 'where possible' may be interpreted in acceptance criteria but does not prevent estimation.

evaluations.evidence: application respond quickly to my actions
evaluations.rationale: No quantitative definition of 'respond quickly' (latency target unspecified) makes it too vague to provide a reasonable implementation estimate.

evaluations.evidence: be able to use Unicode
evaluations.rationale: Supporting Unicode is a definable technical requirement and can be estimated.

evaluations.evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
evaluations.rationale: Although 'sensible' is subjective, producing predictable URL patterns is an actionable design task that can be estimated.

evaluations.evidence: have nice error pages when something goes wrong
evaluations.rationale: Creating error pages is a bounded UI/content task; 'nice' is subjective but does not prevent making an implementation estimate.

evaluations.evidence: results to be stored in a non-identifiable way
evaluations.rationale: 'Non-identifiable' is ambiguous without definition of which data must be anonymized and to what standard, making reasonable estimation difficult.

evaluations.evidence: see some metrics on use of the game
evaluations.rationale: 'Some metrics' is underspecified (which metrics, aggregation, period), leaving scope too vague to reliably estimate implementation effort.
